name: Chairside Atlas
tagline: The Comprehensive Adult Eye Exam, Step by Step
description: A 15-episode walkthrough of every step an optometrist performs during a comprehensive adult eye examination — from history to final prescription — with clinical decision-making at each station.

episodes.title: Master the Clinical History: Maximum Signal in 5 Minutes
episodes.description:
What if your most powerful diagnostic tool isn't a lab test or an imaging scan — it's the conversation you're already having? In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down the art and science of taking a chief complaint and clinical history with maximum efficiency and precision, even when you have five minutes or less.

Studies show that a well-taken history leads to the correct diagnosis 70 to 80 percent of the time before a single test is ordered. Yet the history is one of the most undervalued skills in modern clinical practice. That changes today.

We cover exactly how to open a patient encounter the right way, why letting patients speak uninterrupted for just 60 to 90 seconds transforms the entire visit, and how to use the OLDCARTS framework as a flexible scaffold rather than a rigid script. You will learn the pivot question technique that surfaces hidden patient concerns in seconds, how to listen for what patients are not saying, and why the empathic bridge is one of the most powerful tools in clinical communication. We also walk through how to close the loop with a 30-second summary that catches errors and builds lasting patient trust.

Whether you are a medical student building foundational skills, a resident sharpening your efficiency, or an experienced clinician looking to reconnect with the fundamentals, this episode delivers practical, evidence-based strategies you can apply in your very next patient encounter.

Listen now and start extracting more clinical signal from every conversation. Visit Focuslinks.in to explore more episodes and resources from Focus Cast.

episodes.title: Beyond Snellen: LogMAR, ETDRS & Low-Vision Acuity Testing
episodes.description:
That familiar eye chart on your doctor's wall has been around since 1862 — but is it actually the best way to measure your vision? In this episode of Focus Cast, we pull back the curtain on the science of visual acuity testing and explore why modern eye care has moved far beyond the classic Snellen chart.

We break down exactly what LogMAR means, why its logarithmic scale makes it so much more reliable for tracking vision changes over time, and how the ETDRS chart — born from a landmark diabetic retinopathy study in the 1980s — became the gold standard for ophthalmology research worldwide. You'll learn why researchers can't simply average Snellen fractions, how letter-by-letter ETDRS scoring can detect even the smallest clinically meaningful changes, and why all of this matters when testing new treatments for conditions like macular degeneration.

We also shine a light on an often-overlooked area: measuring vision in people with very low sight. From counting fingers and hand motion to specialized tools like the Feinbloom chart and Lea symbols, discover how clinicians extend the LogMAR scale to capture vision across its full spectrum — because vision isn't binary, and every level of sight deserves to be measured accurately.

Whether you're a curious patient, a student of eye care, or a vision science enthusiast, this episode gives you a genuinely new way to think about something you've done dozens of times without a second thought.

Listen now and visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes covering the fascinating science of how we see the world.

---

episodes.title: Swinging Flashlight Test & Afferent Pupillary Defects Explained
episodes.description:
What can a small flashlight reveal about your optic nerve, neurological health, and even whether vision loss is real or fabricated? More than you'd ever expect. In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we take a deep dive into the swinging flashlight test, one of the most powerful and elegantly simple diagnostic tools in ophthalmology and neurology.

We break down exactly how the pupillary light reflex works, tracing the afferent and efferent pathways that control how your pupils respond to light. Then we walk through the swinging flashlight test step by step, explaining what clinicians are looking for and why a paradoxical pupil dilation is such a significant finding.

You'll learn what a relative afferent pupillary defect, or RAPD, actually means, why it's also called a Marcus Gunn pupil, and what conditions can cause it, including glaucoma, optic neuritis, multiple sclerosis, retinal detachment, central retinal artery occlusion, and compressive optic nerve lesions. We also cover why bilateral optic nerve damage can mask an RAPD, how neutral density filters are used to grade defect severity, and why this test cannot be fooled by efferent problems like a third nerve palsy.

Whether you're a medical student, a healthcare professional, or simply someone curious about how the eyes and brain communicate, this episode gives you a clear, thorough, and genuinely fascinating look at a clinical test that punches well above its weight.

Listen now and discover why your pupils never lie. For more episodes and eye care resources, visit Focuslinks.in.

---

episodes.title: Cover-Uncover Test: Detecting Eye Phorias and Tropias
episodes.description:
Ever noticed an eye that drifts when someone is tired, or a child who squints more on one side? There is a good chance something is happening with their extraocular motility — and a simple clinical tool called the cover-uncover test can reveal exactly what. In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down everything you need to know about how the eyes move, what happens when they do not move together correctly, and how clinicians detect the difference between phorias and tropias.

We start with the six extraocular muscles and the three cranial nerves that control them, explaining how conjugate gaze and binocular vision are supposed to work. From there, we unpack the critical distinction between a tropia — a constant, visible misalignment like esotropia or exotropia — and a phoria, the sneaky latent deviation that only shows itself when fusion is disrupted. You will learn why a decompensated phoria can cause headaches, eye strain, and reading difficulties, and why catching a tropia early in children is so important for preventing amblyopia.

Then we walk through the cover-uncover test step by step, explaining exactly what each part of the test is detecting, how to interpret eye movement, and what the alternate cover test adds to the picture. A real-world clinical scenario ties it all together, showing how this simple test can guide meaningful decisions about treatment.

Whether you are an optometry or ophthalmology student, a clinician refreshing your fundamentals, or simply someone curious about how vision works, this episode gives you a clear, practical understanding of one of eye care's most essential diagnostic techniques. Visit Focuslinks.in to explore more episodes and resources from Focus Cast.

episodes.title: Confrontation Visual Fields: The 2-Minute Screening Test That Saves Lives
episodes.description:
What if a simple two-minute test using just your hands could detect a brain tumor, a stroke, or advanced glaucoma — before a patient even suspects something is wrong? In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we break down confrontation visual fields, one of the most underrated yet powerful screening tools in all of eye care and neurology.

We walk you through exactly how to perform the test, from proper positioning and the finger counting method to the red target technique and the critical extinction test for parietal lobe lesions. You will learn why technique matters, how to avoid common errors, and what different patterns of visual field loss actually mean clinically.

We also decode the major field defect patterns — homonymous hemianopia, bitemporal hemianopia, and quadrantanopias — and explain what each one tells you about where the lesion is hiding in the visual pathway or brain. From pituitary adenomas pressing on the optic chiasm to stroke-related field cuts, confrontation visual fields can be the first clue that changes everything.

Whether you are an optometry student building your clinical foundation, a practicing clinician looking to sharpen your neuro-ophthalmic skills, or simply someone curious about how vision and the brain connect, this episode delivers clear, practical, and genuinely eye-opening insights.

Tune in, take notes, and make confrontation visual fields a non-negotiable part of your clinical routine. Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes and eye care resources, and share this episode with anyone who loves learning about vision science.

episodes.title: Slit Lamp Exam Explained: A Tour of the Anterior Segment
episodes.description:
Ever wondered what your eye doctor is actually seeing when they peer through that futuristic-looking instrument? In this episode of Focus Cast, we take you on a structured, systematic tour of the anterior segment of the eye using slit lamp biomicroscopy — one of the most powerful diagnostic tools in all of clinical medicine.

Starting from the outermost eyelids and working inward to the crystalline lens, we break down exactly what clinicians look for at each stop along the way. Discover how Demodex mites hiding in your lashes can cause chronic blepharitis, why follicles and papillae on the conjunctiva point to completely different diagnoses, and how a simple beam of light can reveal corneal layers, detect herpes simplex keratitis, and expose the earliest signs of Fuchs endothelial dystrophy. We also explore the anterior chamber, where cells and flare signal uveitis, and the lens, where cataract type and density guide surgical decisions.

Whether you are an optometry or ophthalmology student building your clinical foundation, a practitioner refreshing your systematic approach, or simply a curious mind who wants to understand what happens during an eye exam, this episode delivers clear, engaging explanations grounded in real clinical practice.

The slit lamp does not just give you a view — it tells a story. This episode teaches you how to read it.

Tune in, take notes, and the next time you sit at the slit lamp, you will see with entirely new eyes.

Visit us at focuslinks.in for more eye care education, podcast episodes, and clinical resources. If this episode added value to your learning, share it with a colleague or classmate who could benefit.

episodes.title: Tonometry Explained: Goldmann vs iCare vs Rebound
episodes.description:
What actually happens when a doctor measures your eye pressure — and why does it matter so much? In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down tonometry, one of the most critical yet misunderstood tests in eye care, by comparing three of the most widely used methods: Goldmann Applanation Tonometry, iCare, and Rebound Tonometry.

We start with the basics — what intraocular pressure is, how it connects to glaucoma, and why catching elevated IOP early can literally save your sight. Then we dive deep into each method. You will learn how Goldmann Applanation Tonometry became the gold standard using the Imbert-Fick principle, why it still leads clinical decision-making after six decades, and where its limitations lie. We then explore the iCare tonometer — a handheld, anesthetic-free device that is transforming how eye pressure is measured in children, bedside patients, and even at home. Finally, we zoom out to understand rebound tonometry as a broader technology, covering its origins, its elegant physics, and why it has expanded access to IOP measurement across pediatric care, veterinary medicine, and resource-limited settings.

Whether you are an optometry or ophthalmology student, a practicing clinician, or simply someone who wants to understand what goes on at your eye appointment, this episode gives you a clear, practical, and genuinely interesting look at how we measure one of the most important numbers in eye health.

Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes, resources, and eye care content designed to make complex topics accessible and actionable.

episodes.title: Gonioscopy: Indications, Technique & Angle Grading Explained
episodes.description:
Can you truly evaluate glaucoma without looking directly into the anterior chamber angle? The answer is no — and that's exactly why gonioscopy is one of the most essential skills in ophthalmology. In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down everything clinicians and students need to know about gonioscopy, from the optical principles that make it possible to the hands-on technique that makes it reliable.

We start with the indications — broader than most learners expect — covering elevated intraocular pressure, shallow anterior chambers, pigment dispersion syndrome, pseudoexfoliation, traumatic angle recession, and neovascular glaucoma. Next, we walk through the technique step by step, comparing direct and indirect gonioscopy, explaining the Goldmann three-mirror and Zeiss four-mirror lenses, and demystifying dynamic indentation gonioscopy and why it matters for distinguishing appositional from synechial angle closure.

Then we tackle angle grading, covering both the Shaffer grading system and the more detailed Spaeth grading system, along with how to identify key anatomical landmarks including Schwalbe's line, the trabecular meshwork, the scleral spur, and the ciliary body band. We also discuss trabecular meshwork pigmentation grading and share clinical pearls that can sharpen your diagnostic accuracy right away.

Whether you're a resident building foundational skills or an experienced clinician looking for a structured refresher, this episode gives you a clear, practical framework for performing and interpreting gonioscopy with confidence. Listen now, and visit Focuslinks.in for more ophthalmology episodes and clinical resources.

---

episodes.title: Fundus Evaluation: Direct vs Indirect vs Slit Lamp Hruby
episodes.description:
Ever wondered what your doctor actually sees when they shine that bright light into your eye? In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down the three essential methods of fundus evaluation — direct ophthalmoscopy, indirect ophthalmoscopy, and slit lamp biomicroscopy with the Hruby lens — so you can understand not just how each technique works, but when and why a clinician chooses one over another.

We start with direct ophthalmoscopy, the classic handheld tool that delivers a magnified, upright view of the optic disc but a frustratingly narrow field of view. Then we move to binocular indirect ophthalmoscopy, the gold standard for peripheral retinal examination, offering a wide field of view that makes it indispensable for detecting retinal detachments, peripheral tears, and retinopathy of prematurity. Finally, we explore slit lamp biomicroscopy with the Hruby lens, a powerful method for detailed, stereoscopic evaluation of the posterior pole, including the macula and optic disc.

Whether you are a medical student picking up the ophthalmoscope for the first time, an optometry student preparing for clinical exams, or a practising clinician looking to sharpen your fundus examination skills, this episode gives you a clear, practical framework for understanding these three techniques side by side.

By the end, you will know exactly which tool belongs in which clinical situation — and why that decision matters for your patients.

Listen now and take your fundus examination knowledge to the next level. Visit Focuslinks.in for more ophthalmology and optometry resources, and subscribe to Focus Cast so you never miss an episode.

episodes.title: Retinoscopy Explained: Neutralising the Reflex for Objective Refraction
episodes.description:
What if you could determine someone's exact prescription without them saying a single word? That is precisely what retinoscopy makes possible, and in this episode of Focus Cast, we break down one of optometry's most powerful and enduring clinical skills.

We explore how retinoscopy works from the ground up, starting with how a streak of light projected into the eye reflects back to reveal its refractive state. You will learn what "with" and "against" movements mean, why the moment of neutralisation is the key to unlocking an objective refraction, and how to account for working distance when calculating your final result.

We also dive deep into astigmatism, explaining how different meridians behave under the retinoscope and how the cross-cylinder technique allows you to neutralise each meridian separately for a complete refractive picture. We cover the scissors reflex, what it signals clinically, and why cycloplegic retinoscopy is essential in paediatric practice.

Whether you are a student picking up a retinoscope for the first time or an experienced clinician looking to refine your technique, this episode offers practical tips on controlling working distance, reading reflex quality, and developing the kind of intuitive skill that no automated refractor can replicate.

Retinoscopy is not just a historical technique. It is a clinical lifeline for patients who cannot participate in standard subjective refraction, from young children to individuals with cognitive disabilities.

If you are serious about mastering objective refraction, this episode is essential listening. Share it with a classmate or colleague, and visit Focuslinks dot in for more episodes and clinical resources to support your growth in eye care.

---

episodes.title: Subjective Refraction Explained: MPMRA, JCC & Duochrome Test
episodes.description:
Ever wondered what's really happening when your eye doctor flips lenses and asks, "Which is better, one or two?" In this episode of Focus Cast, we pull back the curtain on subjective refraction and break down three of its most essential techniques: the MPMRA, the Jackson Cross Cylinder, and the Duochrome test.

We start with the MPMRA, or Maximum Plus to Maximum Visual Acuity, explaining why finding the least amount of minus power matters and how over-minusing can lead to eye strain and fatigue. Next, we dive deep into the Jackson Cross Cylinder, the century-old tool still considered the gold standard for refining astigmatic correction. You will learn exactly how it is used to fine-tune both cylinder axis and power, and why its bracketing principle makes it so reliable. Finally, we explore the Duochrome test, a clever technique rooted in the physics of chromatic aberration that helps clinicians confirm the perfect spherical endpoint with speed and precision.

Whether you are an optometry or ophthalmology student trying to master clinical refraction, a practising clinician looking to sharpen your technique, or simply someone curious about the science behind your eye exam, this episode gives you a clear, logical, and engaging walkthrough of the entire process.

By the end, you will understand not just what each test does, but why it works, and how the three techniques work together as a seamless, systematic sequence. Visit Focuslinks.in for more vision science content, articles, and resources to support your learning journey.

---

episodes.title: Binocular Balance & Near Add Determination Explained
episodes.description:
What separates a good refraction from a truly great one? In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we dive deep into two of the most clinically important yet underappreciated concepts in optometry — binocular balance and near add determination. Whether you're a student stepping into your first refraction lab, a seasoned clinician looking to sharpen your technique, or simply someone curious about what really happens during an eye exam, this episode breaks it all down in plain, engaging language.

We explore why binocular balance matters, how unequal accommodative demand between the two eyes can cause headaches, eye strain, and patient dissatisfaction — and how to fix it. We walk through the most widely used balancing techniques, including prism dissociation, alternate occlusion, and the Humphriss Immediate Contrast method, explaining when and why each one works best.

Then we shift to near add determination — the science and art of prescribing the right reading addition for presbyopic patients. From Donders' table and the addition range method to push-up amplitude testing and the near duochrome test, we cover the clinical tools that help you dial in a comfortable, personalized near prescription. We also discuss why understanding a patient's real-world visual demands matters just as much as the measurements themselves.

If you want to understand how both eyes are brought into harmony across all working distances — and why that process is so central to patient satisfaction — this episode is essential listening.

Visit us at Focuslinks.in for more episodes and vision care resources. Don't forget to share this episode with a colleague or student who'd find it valuable.

---

episodes.title: Colour Vision & Contrast Sensitivity Testing Explained
episodes.description:
Did you know that up to 8% of men have a colour vision deficiency — and many don't even know it? In this episode of Focus Cast, we take a deep dive into two of the most underutilised tests in clinical optometry: colour vision testing and contrast sensitivity testing. Together, they reveal far more about how a patient truly sees the world than a standard acuity chart ever could.

We start with the science of how the eye perceives colour, breaking down trichromatic vision, the difference between colour blindness and colour vision deficiency, and why this distinction matters both clinically and practically. From there, we walk through the key testing tools used in practice — the Ishihara colour plates, the Farnsworth-Munsell 100 Hue Test, and the Farnsworth D-15 — explaining what each one measures and where its limitations lie.

Then we shift to contrast sensitivity, exploring why a patient can ace the letter chart and still struggle to drive at night, navigate a staircase in dim light, or spot a pedestrian on a foggy road. We cover how conditions like cataracts, glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and multiple sclerosis can silently erode contrast sensitivity long before acuity is affected — and how tools like the Pelli-Robson chart can help you catch what a standard eye exam might miss.

Whether you are an optometry student, a practising clinician, or simply someone curious about the science of sight, this episode will change the way you think about visual assessment.

Listen now and discover why complete vision care goes far beyond reading the bottom line of a chart. Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes and resources.

---

episodes.title: Vertex Distance, Prism & Patient Counsel: Final Prescription Guide
episodes.description:
What separates a technically correct prescription from one that truly works for your patient? In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we go beyond sphere, cylinder, and axis to explore three critical elements that every optometrist and optician must master before a patient walks out the door.

We start with vertex distance — why it matters more than most practitioners realize, how a few millimeters can shift the effective power of a high-powered lens, and how to compensate for it when your patient's frame sits differently than your phoropter. Then we dive into prism prescription, breaking down how prism diopters work, when to prescribe base-in versus base-out prism, and why split prism can make all the difference in patient comfort. We even walk through a real-world case of a patient whose chronic headaches and eye strain were completely resolved with a small but targeted prism correction.

Finally, we tackle the most underestimated skill in clinical practice — patient counseling. From explaining prescriptions in plain language to setting realistic adaptation expectations for progressive lens wearers, we cover exactly what to say and why it matters. Research shows that patients who receive clear, confident explanations from their eye care providers actually report better visual outcomes. Your words are part of the prescription.

Whether you are a seasoned optometrist, an optician, or an optometry student looking to sharpen your clinical thinking, this episode gives you practical, actionable insights you can apply immediately.

Listen now and transform the way you write — and communicate — your final prescriptions. Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes and resources on optics and eye care.
